attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his signed post. It is not a quotation of anyone else.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps 'and so' as a causal link and keeps 'on a path to … zero' as written. The scope matches the systems the post discusses. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Reading the claim as negligible marginal cost per item is ordinary and fair. Separating provider cost from customer price is reasonable. The Nov–Dec 2022 window was chosen by the evaluator, not the speaker, but it fits the present-tense framing.

evidence.note: Company CEO's tentative estimate of a few cents per chat. It is small but above zero, does not define its cost components, and does not measure the cost of producing disinformation.
Free preview access is a customer price, not an operating cost. It does not bear on the causal mechanism.

Later fall in inference prices (2022–2024), published before the evaluation date. It covers a different period and measures customer prices, not provider operating costs or total disinformation-production cost.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows small per-chat costs and later price declines. Nothing measures the full cost of producing disinformation, or shows that cheap model operation is pushing that cost toward negligible levels. The causal claim is neither established nor refuted by this evidence.

attribution.note: Marcus's own bullet point in his signed post.

semantics.note: 'Can easily be automated' is a present-tense statement of capability, not a hedge about probability. Treating it as an observation is correct, and the scope matches the post.

contract.note: The readings of 'easily' (little effort per added item) and 'unprecedented' (compared with earlier production methods) are ordinary. The evaluator chose the period, and that choice is reasonable.

evidence.note: 2021 GPT-3 experiments: a human-machine team could produce thousands of messages a day, with human curation. This predates the target period and uses a different system, so it is background only.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is an earlier GPT-3 study. It points toward high-volume generation with modest effort, but it is not a measurement of the systems in Nov–Dec 2022 against a stated historical baseline. The packet does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his signed post. The quoted Stack Overflow policy is separate, and this claim does not rest on it.

semantics.note: The conditional keeps its antecedent, and the firm 'will' makes it a scored forecast. 'Generated' code is a fair reading in context. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Reading 'die' as closure of the service is a plain reading. Marking the antecedent as met is debatable, because the temporary ban may have stopped a sustained flood. Either way the result here is unresolved.

evidence.note: A moderator's firsthand account from Dec 2022 of thousands of ChatGPT answers. It is evidence for the antecedent, not for the predicted outcome.
Company survey published Oct 2026: users report lower participation but continued use. It shows no closure and does not attribute the decline to erroneous generated content.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. The packet shows no closure event, so the early-resolution rule is not met, and a site that is still running with lower participation does not contradict an open-ended forecast. The forecast cannot be scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his signed post.

semantics.note: 'Almost certain' expresses high confidence in a definite outcome, so under the policy it is a scored forecast, not a hedged one. No deadline is stated.

contract.note: Reading 'society overrun' as broad exposure or disruption, not just the existence of content farms, is ordinary and fair. 'Tidal wave' has no threshold, so interpretation matters.

evidence.note: Early baseline of 49 AI content-farm sites (Apr 2023). Most of them were not spreading misinformation.
Tracker counts 3,749 AI content-farm sites as of June 2026. It counts sites, not audience exposure or how much of the content is false.
OpenAI's disclosure about its own investigations (2024): AI-assisted influence operations got little authentic engagement. This qualifies the claim but does not decisively refute it.

reviews.rationale: There is no deadline. Growth in AI content farms continues, but nothing in the packet shows broad, society-wide exposure or disruption, which is the threshold for support. Nothing makes the outcome impossible either. The early-resolution rule is not met.
